finding.claim: The DELETE /projects/:id handler calls authorized(), which returns a boolean, and discards the result. Any authenticated user can delete any project, including projects owned by other users.
finding.source: Authenticated non-owner, non-admin user sends DELETE /projects/<victim project id>.

trace.note: Project is fetched by req.params.id with no ownership scoping.
authorized(req.user, project) returns false for a non-owner, but the return value is ignored and nothing is thrown.
authorized() only returns a boolean. Unlike authorize() at line 4, it never throws.

finding.guards_checked: Checked authorize() at line 4, which throws on failure but is not the function called here. Checked authorized() at line 12, which returns false but whose result is unused. Found no other middleware or checks in this file. Authentication of req.user is assumed to happen upstream. Even then, the per-resource ownership check is missing.

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean, but its result is discarded at api.js:18. authorize() at api.js:4 throws, but only the PUT handler calls it (api.js:25). No other middleware exists in this file or directory, since api.js is the only file.
verdict.reason: api.js:18 calls authorized() as a bare statement and ignores the boolean, so api.js:19 deletes any project for any authenticated user. The PUT handler at api.js:25 shows the intended throwing authorize() was not used here.
